page: Amazon Web Services hpc6a.48xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server designed for high-performance computing workloads. It features 96 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running at 3.6 GHz, with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. It utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and includes a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory operations. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Passmark CPU metrics (including physics, encryption, and extended instructions), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks also ranks in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression tasks scoring in the middle 50%.

The lack of local storage and GPU accelerators limits this server's utility for direct database hosting or hardware-accelerated deep learning. This is reflected in the LLM inference benchmarks, where text generation for a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 25%. Conversely, the high physical core count and 100 Gbps network throughput make it highly efficient for parallel compute-intensive tasks. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, ray tracing, molecular dynamics, weather modeling, and other highly parallel engineering simulations.
